text:
The diff removes 10.101.1.0/24 (the tenantA-web subnet, where web-a1 lives) from PL_PUBLIC on both borders, so the announcement of that prefix to the WAN stops. Tenant B's web subnet is 10.201.1.0/24, which stays in the list. The ticket says "tenant B", but the diff actually withdraws tenant A's web prefix, so the tests check what the diff really does and also guard that tenant B's announcement stays in place.

The `wan` router holds the announced routes, so it is the right place to check for the prefix being present or absent. The reachability tests check that internal reachability for web-a1 is unchanged, since only the WAN advertisement should change. They also check that tenant B web stays reachable from the WAN.

```json
{"tests": [
  {"t":"route","dev":"wan","prefix":"10.101.1.0/24","expect":"absent"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"wan","prefix":"10.201.1.0/24","expect":"present"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"web-a1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"web-a1","svc":"tcp/80","expect":"deny"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"web-b1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"allow"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"web-b1","svc":"tcp/80","expect":"allow"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"border1","prefix":"10.101.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"border2","prefix":"10.101.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"border1","prefix":"10.201.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"border2","prefix":"10.201.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"app-a1","dst":"web-a1","svc":"tcp/443","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"web-a1","svc":"tcp/22","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-a1","dst":"dns-dc1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-a1","dst":"db-a1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-b1","dst":"dns-dc1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"web-b1","dst":"db-b1","svc":"tcp/5432","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"stage-a1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"stage-b1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"db-a1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"wan-user1","dst":"db-b1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"border1","b":"wan","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"border2","b":"wan","expect":"unchanged"}
]}
```

**Note for the change owner:** the ticket says tenant B's web servers, but the diff removes 10.101.1.0/24, which is tenant A's web subnet. Tenant B's prefix (10.201.1.0/24) is untouched. If the intent was to stop announcing tenant B, the diff targets the wrong prefix, and the tests above (WAN reaching web-a1 denied, WAN reaching web-b1 allowed) will make that mismatch visible.
